text: The patient was admitted with fever, productive cough, and shortness of breath for four days. Examination suggested a lower respiratory tract infection. Chest X-ray showed patchy right lower zone infiltrates. Intravenous antibiotics, nebulization, and oxygen support were started. Over the next two days, oxygen requirement decreased and fever settled. The patient was discharged on oral antibiotics with advice for hydration, breathing exercises, and review in one week.
summary: The report describes a lower respiratory tract infection with cough, fever, and breathing difficulty. Imaging supported infection, treatment was given with antibiotics and oxygen, and the patient improved before discharge with follow-up advice.

text: A 58-year-old patient presented with headache, dizziness, and elevated blood pressure readings at home. Blood pressure in clinic was 182 over 104 mmHg. There was no focal neurological deficit on examination. ECG did not show acute ischemic changes. Antihypertensive medication dose was adjusted and salt restriction was advised. The patient was asked to monitor blood pressure twice daily and return for follow-up in five days.
summary: The patient had poorly controlled hypertension with headache and dizziness but no acute ECG changes. Medication was adjusted, lifestyle advice was given, and close blood pressure follow-up was recommended.

text: The laboratory panel showed fasting blood sugar of 186 milligrams per deciliter and HbA1c of 8.9 percent. Serum creatinine was within normal range. Lipid profile showed mildly elevated triglycerides. The findings were discussed with the patient. Diet control, exercise, and medication review were advised. Repeat glucose monitoring was recommended.
summary: The report shows poorly controlled diabetes with elevated fasting glucose and HbA1c. Kidney function was normal, triglycerides were mildly high, and lifestyle plus medication review were advised.

text: Ultrasound abdomen was performed for abdominal pain. The liver was mildly enlarged with increased echogenicity consistent with fatty infiltration. Gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen appeared unremarkable. No ascites was seen. Impression stated mild fatty liver changes. Clinical correlation and liver function review were advised.
summary: The ultrasound showed mild fatty liver changes without other major abdominal abnormalities. Clinical correlation and liver function review were advised.

text: The patient was admitted with chest pain and sweating. Initial ECG showed nonspecific ST-T changes. Serial troponin levels were negative. Blood pressure was elevated on admission. Pain improved with medical management and observation. The patient remained hemodynamically stable and was discharged with antihypertensive therapy, antacid medication, and cardiology follow-up.
summary: The patient was observed for chest pain, but serial troponins were negative and no definite acute infarction was confirmed. Symptoms improved with treatment, and discharge medications with cardiology follow-up were advised.

text: A patient with known asthma presented with wheezing and night cough for three days. Oxygen saturation was 95 percent on room air. Bilateral expiratory wheeze was heard on auscultation. Nebulized bronchodilator and inhaled steroid therapy were reinforced. Trigger avoidance and inhaler technique counseling were provided. Follow-up was advised if symptoms worsened or did not improve within three days.
summary: The note describes an asthma flare with wheeze and cough but stable oxygen saturation. Bronchodilator and inhaled steroid treatment were reinforced, and the patient was counseled on trigger avoidance and follow-up.

text: Complete blood count showed hemoglobin of 8.7 grams per deciliter with microcytic hypochromic indices. White blood cell count and platelet count were normal. Peripheral smear suggested iron deficiency anemia. Iron studies were recommended for confirmation. Oral iron therapy and dietary advice were suggested.
summary: The blood tests indicate microcytic anemia likely due to iron deficiency. Other cell lines were normal, and iron studies plus iron replacement advice were given.

text: Chest X-ray was obtained for persistent cough. Cardiomediastinal silhouette was within normal limits. Mild bibasal linear atelectatic changes were noted. No focal consolidation or pleural effusion was seen. Impression stated no acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
summary: The chest X-ray did not show an acute cardiopulmonary problem. Mild bibasal atelectatic changes were noted without focal pneumonia or pleural effusion.

text: The patient was admitted with acute gastroenteritis causing vomiting and loose stools. Clinical dehydration was noted at presentation. Intravenous fluids and antiemetics were administered. Stool frequency reduced over 24 hours and oral intake improved. The patient was discharged on oral rehydration, light diet, and warning signs education.
summary: The patient was treated for acute gastroenteritis with dehydration using fluids and antiemetics. Symptoms improved, and discharge advice included oral rehydration, diet care, and warning signs.

text: A patient complained of burning urination and urinary frequency for two days. There was no flank pain or fever. Urine routine showed pyuria. Oral antibiotics, hydration, and urine culture were advised. The patient was instructed to return if fever or back pain developed.
summary: The note is consistent with a lower urinary tract infection without systemic features. Pyuria was present, antibiotics and hydration were advised, and the patient was told to watch for worsening symptoms.

text: Renal function tests showed serum creatinine of 2.1 milligrams per deciliter and blood urea of 64 milligrams per deciliter. Estimated glomerular filtration rate was reduced. Potassium was mildly elevated. The findings were explained as abnormal kidney function requiring prompt review. Nephrology consultation and repeat renal panel were advised.
summary: The laboratory results show impaired kidney function with elevated creatinine and urea, reduced eGFR, and mild hyperkalemia. Prompt nephrology review and repeat testing were advised.

text: MRI brain was performed for recurrent headache. No acute infarct, hemorrhage, or mass lesion was identified. Mild chronic small vessel ischemic changes were seen. Ventricular system was normal in size. Impression stated no acute intracranial abnormality.
summary: The MRI brain showed no acute intracranial abnormality. Mild chronic small vessel ischemic changes were noted.

text: The patient was treated for cellulitis of the left leg with redness, swelling, and pain. Doppler study ruled out deep vein thrombosis. Intravenous antibiotics were given for two days. Local swelling reduced and pain improved. The patient was discharged on oral antibiotics with leg elevation and wound review advice.
summary: The patient had left leg cellulitis and deep vein thrombosis was excluded on Doppler. Antibiotic treatment improved symptoms, and discharge advice included oral medication, leg elevation, and follow-up.

text: A diabetic patient reported tingling and burning sensation in both feet. Foot examination showed no ulcer or active infection. Blood sugar logs suggested poor glycemic control. Neuropathy symptoms were discussed, medication adherence was reinforced, and foot care advice was given. Follow-up with glucose review was planned.
summary: The note suggests diabetic peripheral neuropathy symptoms without foot ulceration. Blood sugar control appeared poor, and counseling focused on medication adherence, foot care, and follow-up.

text: Thyroid profile revealed thyroid stimulating hormone of 11.2 with low free T4. Hemoglobin and creatinine were within normal range. Findings were consistent with hypothyroidism. Thyroid medication review and repeat thyroid function testing after treatment adjustment were advised.
summary: The labs are consistent with hypothyroidism based on elevated TSH and low free T4. Other basic parameters were normal, and thyroid treatment review with repeat testing was advised.

text: X-ray knee was performed for chronic pain. Mild medial compartment joint space narrowing and small osteophytes were present. No acute fracture or dislocation was seen. Impression favored early osteoarthritic changes.
summary: The knee X-ray showed early osteoarthritic changes with mild joint space narrowing and osteophytes. No acute bony injury was seen.

text: The patient was admitted for symptomatic hypoglycemia with sweating and tremor. Capillary glucose at presentation was 48 milligrams per deciliter. Dextrose was administered and symptoms improved rapidly. Home diabetes medications were reviewed and dosing errors were suspected. The patient was discharged after observation with dietary counseling and medication adjustment advice.
summary: The patient had symptomatic hypoglycemia that improved after dextrose. Medication dosing was reviewed, and discharge advice included dietary counseling and treatment adjustment.

text: A patient presented with low back pain radiating to the right leg after lifting weight. There was no bowel or bladder disturbance. Straight leg raising was mildly positive on the right side. Analgesics, rest, posture advice, and physiotherapy referral were given. MRI was advised only if weakness or persistent symptoms developed.
summary: The note describes mechanical low back pain with right-sided radicular features but no red flag bowel or bladder symptoms. Conservative treatment and physiotherapy were advised, with MRI only if symptoms persisted or worsened.

text: Liver function tests showed elevated alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase with normal bilirubin. Albumin was within normal range. Viral hepatitis markers were negative. The pattern was discussed as likely nonviral liver injury requiring further clinical correlation. Repeat liver function and metabolic review were advised.
summary: The laboratory results show elevated liver enzymes with normal bilirubin and negative viral hepatitis markers. Further clinical correlation and repeat liver function review were advised.

text: CT abdomen was performed for renal colic. A 4 millimeter calculus was seen in the distal right ureter with mild upstream hydroureter. No large obstructing stone was seen elsewhere. Impression stated right distal ureteric stone. Urology review and hydration were advised.
summary: The CT abdomen identified a small right distal ureteric stone with mild upstream dilatation. Urology review and hydration were advised.
